title: Finite countermodels and decidability for weak excluded middle

based_on.title: Intuitionistic Logic, Winter 2019/20 (notes dated January 2, 2020)
based_on.pages: §1.8 and §2, printed pp.25–29; finite geometric tracing developed locally

based_on.title: Filtration (March 14, 2012)
based_on.pages: Entire page; corrected closure and untracked-atom conventions

summary: Preserve a least root and greatest world through filtration, then decide finite KC consequence by a bounded scan of class-checked model tables.
abstract: Weak excluded middle permits more proofs than intuitionistic logic while still failing to prove ordinary excluded middle. To decide a finite problem in this logic, a finite countermodel must satisfy its extra frame condition as well as the required formula tests. We filter the rooted directed canonical countermodel, keeping its least root and obtaining a greatest world in the finite frame. That greatest world validates every weak excluded middle instance, including those outside the finite tracked set. A bound from the input subformulas then makes an exhaustive table search possible. Checking its relation, valuation and endpoints turns a passing candidate into a countermodel, while the filtered model ensures that every failed deduction has a passing candidate.
